summary: Step M2-S05 (access, owner metadata-builder) executed and set built. build_plan.py next returned it as the only runnable step, its step:M2-S05 human gate is approved, and set-status running was accepted. The owning agent is build-aware (grep count 39), so its Plan was executed inline per Step 6's non-Claude-Code clause at the caller's instruction and it wrote directly under artefacts/M2-S05/ - no relocation was needed. Four declared outputs written, zero undeclared files, zero files outside the step's artefact directory. check-outputs ok. Both envelopes validate.
confidence_rationale: Step 9's HIGH row is met on every mechanical condition - the step was in next, every required input of the owning agent resolved from the plan, both envelopes validate, check-outputs exited 0, and nothing was written outside artefacts/M2-S05/. It is held at MEDIUM for one reason the HIGH row does not cover and the runner will not paper over: the owning agent's own envelope returned MEDIUM, and a runner cannot be more confident in a step than the agent that built it. The owning agent's optional api_version input also had no plan-level value and was resolved to 62.0 from the sibling manifests - Step 9's MEDIUM row names exactly that case.

inputs_received.note: No credential-shaped value appeared in the step's inputs{}, in the bound clarifications (Q13, Q80) or in requirement.md, so nothing required [REDACTED] treatment.

dimensions_skipped.reason: The runner does not own the step's molecular tests - step-tester does, per standards/build-orchestration.md section 5. The step's declared checker command was nevertheless run verbatim from the build directory as evidence for the built transition, because check-outputs alone cannot tell a well-formed sharing rule from one that grants nothing. The xml and manifest always-on checks and the manual test were not run.
dimensions_skipped.retry_hint: Run /test-build-step M2-S05; the manual test is ticked by a human at the M2 gate from the artefacts on disk.

process_observations.observation: The amend-step that added deploy-order.md to this step's outputs[] did its job: this is the first M2 step where the deploy-order note is a declared output check-outputs actually confirms, rather than a file the owning agent writes on every run that no reader of plan.json can see.

The step:M2-S05 human gate did the work a gate exists for - set-status running was accepted only because a human had approved it first, and this step is exactly the irreversible-if-wrong kind (record access) the gate is meant to catch.

The step's declared manifest acceptance test hard-codes one of the two manifest forms the library documents for a sharing-rules file ('SharingRules:Case as its own <name> block'), which means the plan, not the skill, decided a metadata question - and the skill the step cites recommends the other form.

plan.json carries no api_version field at all, so every metadata-builder step has resolved 62.0 from its own default or from a sibling manifest; five steps have now independently reached the same value, which works until one of them does not.

The invoking instruction described this step as building 'the criteria-based sharing rule(s) that let Billing see Billing cases', while the step's own declared manual acceptance test asserts that the only rule shares Support cases to Support_Tier_2 and that no rule names the Billing record type or Billing_Team; the runner followed the plan, which is the artefact the tester and the gate read, and is flagging the divergence rather than resolving it.
M2-S05 is at built; its declared checker, xml, manifest and manual tests have not been run by their owner.
process_observations.followup_reason: It runs the step's molecular tests and writes tests/M2-S05/results.json, which set-status tested requires and this agent must not write.

process_observations.observation: M2-S05 is the last pending step in M2; once it is tested and documented the milestone gate becomes decidable.
